Saving and sharing analysis recipes

Source: vignettes/import_export_recipes.Rmd
import_export_recipes.Rmd

export_steps() saves an analysis configuration; import_steps() restores it onto data supplied by the user. The versioned, non-executable dar-recipe JSON format stores the central model, ordered preprocessing and differential abundance steps, their identifiers and native options. Optional consensus configurations are stored separately when exporting a prepared recipe.

The file does not contain the input data, fitted results, active random-number state or software environment. Sharing the JSON alone therefore does not guarantee identical results on another computer.

Save a configuration

This example configures an analysis without fitting a model. The temporary path keeps the example self-contained; use a persistent path when saving a recipe for later work.

data(metaHIV_phy)

configured <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(
    ~ RiskGroup2,
    targets = "RiskGroup2",
    tax_level = "Species"
  ) |>
  step_subset_taxa(tax_level = "Kingdom", taxa = c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) |>
  step_filter_by_prevalence(threshold = 0.03) |>
  step_maaslin()

recipe_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
export_steps(configured, recipe_file)

The model record includes references, contrasts, the missing-value policy and any time settings. See Statistical models and contrasts for configuring those fields.

Restore onto data

Start with a new recipe containing the intended data. The JSON supplies the model and steps; importing this file does not run the analysis.

restored <- import_steps(recipe(metaHIV_phy), recipe_file)
get_model(restored)
#> $formula
#> ~RiskGroup2
#> <environment: base>
#> 
#> $targets
#> [1] "RiskGroup2"
#> 
#> $tax_level
#> [1] "Species"
#> 
#> $time
#> NULL
#> 
#> $reference
#> NULL
#> 
#> $contrasts
#> [1] "simple"
#> 
#> $na_action
#> [1] "error"
#> 
#> $max_time_levels
#> [1] 12
steps_ids(restored)
#> [1] "subset_taxa__Ensaïmada"              
#> [2] "filter_by_prevalence__Puff_pastry"   
#> [3] "maaslin__Fazuelos_Fijuelas_or_Deblas"

Using other data reuses the configuration, not the original analysis. Check that the required metadata, factor levels, reference categories and taxonomic ranks are present and appropriate for the new study.

Run prep() explicitly when ready. Set the execution seed immediately before the run; it is not restored from the JSON:

set.seed(130)
results <- prep(restored, parallel = FALSE)
tidy_results(results)

bake() is not required to execute a recipe or inspect its per-method results. If an exported file does contain consensus configurations, importing it into an unprepared recipe requires explicit prepare = TRUE; otherwise import stops without fitting models. The parallel and workers arguments apply only to that explicit preparation path. Importing into an already prepared recipe requires its model and analysis steps to match the file.

What to archive alongside the recipe

For a reproducible handoff, keep the input data and preprocessing provenance, the execution script with its seed and execution settings, fitted results, and the R, dar and engine-package versions. sessionInfo() records loaded versions; an environment lockfile or container can additionally preserve the dependencies. Stochastic methods and execution settings can affect results even when the recipe parameters match.

Recipe files are treated as untrusted data: constructors, fields, formulas and filter predicates are validated against explicit allowlists before the recipe is changed. R functions in engine_args are not serializable. Legacy executable exports are rejected; recreate their configuration using the current API and export it again rather than executing an old recipe file.
